title: Memento
about: A man who can't make new memories hunts his wife's killer with Polaroids, notes and tattoos, and the story runs backwards.
cue: Serve the steak when Jimmy offers Leonard the 200 grand in the car.
faces: Instant Polaroid grilled cheese with tomato soup

Three cheeses pressed flat, a shot of soup.How to make it1 tbsp olive oil1 brown onion, diced2 garlic cloves, sliced800g tinned whole tomatoes250ml vegetable stock60ml pouring cream8 slices of white sandwich bread40g butter, softened100g vintage cheddar, grated100g mozzarella, grated30g parmesan, finely gratedSoften the onion and garlic in the oil, add the tomatoes and stock and simmer for 15 minutes.Blend smooth, stir in the cream and season.Butter the outsides of the bread, fill with the cheddar and mozzarella, and press the parmesan onto the buttered sides.Cook in a pan under a weight until crisp and melting, then trim into neat squares like little Polaroids and serve with shot glasses of soup.Room 304 loaded nachosBurt rents Leonard a second room. Corn chips, black beans, cheddar, jalapeno.How to make it230g bag plain corn chips400g tin black beans, drained1 tsp ground cumin150g cheddar, grated2 tomatoes, diced1/2 red onion, finely diced1 lime2 tbsp pickled jalapenos125g sour cream1 avocadoWarm the beans with the cumin and a splash of water, mashing a few.Mix the tomato and red onion with half the lime juice and a pinch of salt.Layer the chips, beans and cheese twice in a baking dish and bake at 200°C until the cheese bubbles.Mash the avocado with the rest of the lime, then top the nachos with salsa, jalapenos, avocado and sour cream.Motel mints on the pillowLeonard won't remember eating them.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.Blue PlatesTwo hundred grand steak frites with peppercorn sauceJimmy's cash in the Jaguar's trunk. Rib-eye, green peppercorn sauce, fries.How to make it4 x 250g rib-eye steaks1kg floury potatoes, cut in thin chips1 L vegetable oil, for frying30g butter1 French shallot, finely diced2 tbsp green peppercorns in brine, drained60ml brandy200ml thickened cream1 tsp Dijon mustardFry the chips at 150°C until soft but pale, then lift out and drain.Season the steaks and sear in a very hot pan for 3 to 4 minutes a side for medium rare, then rest.Melt the butter in the steak pan, soften the shallot and peppercorns, add the brandy and let it bubble off.Add the cream and mustard and simmer until it coats a spoon.Fry the chips again at 190°C until crisp, salt them and serve with the steak and sauce.Pie and SweetsBackwards pineapple upside-down cakeThe colour scenes run in reverse. Caramel pineapple, cherries, vanilla cream.How to make it60g butter, melted, plus 125g softened100g brown sugar440g tin pineapple rings, drained8 glace cherries150g caster sugar2 eggs1 tsp vanilla extract185g self-raising flour125ml milk200ml thickened cream, whippedPour the melted butter into a 22cm cake tin, scatter over the brown sugar and lay the pineapple rings on top with a cherry in each hole.Beat the softened butter and caster sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs and vanilla.Fold in the flour and milk and spread the batter over the fruit.Bake at 180°C until a skewer comes out clean.Rest for 5 minutes, turn out upside down and serve warm with the cream.From Ferdy's BarBourbon-back boilermakerHe drinks it even after Natalie spits in it.
